readings_ruling: The dispatch asked five questions. (1) The Déf. 6 mark is faithful and consistent. It should stay (label notes). (2) Prop. 5's r ≤ 0 finding. The Lean is right, but the claim about the paper is not established and is probably false (finding 1). ouvertPleinPrinted_iff is correctly proved and has the printed shape. But at r ≤ 0 it quantifies over pseudoBoule, which the Lean extends to every real radius. Déf. 6 defines a pseudo-ball only for « r un nombre réel positif ». The REPORT says r = 0 is « positif », but the paper's own usage reads « positif » as > 0. So, under the paper's convention, Prop. 5's « pseudo-boule … de rayon r » carries r > 0, and ouvert_plein is Prop. 5 as printed. (3) The two readings of the unlabelled sentences. Neither is a narrowing. « connexe » with ∅ (IsPreconnected) is the weaker conclusion, but isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff proves the non-empty form exactly where it can hold (n ≥ 1, r > 0) and refutes it elsewhere. Under either reading, the Lean is therefore at least the paper. Under the paper's « positif » = > 0, the reading matters only in dimension 0, which is OQ-45 (finding 3). « de rayon quelconque » read as r > 0 is, under the paper's convention, simply Déf. 6's radii. Under Bourbaki's convention it drops only r = 0, whose ball ∅ is no neighbourhood, so the sentence could not otherwise be true. That is the evident reading, and it is not a narrowing. (4) Exactly one bold label mark exists in the file: **`bzdef:c2s2d6_pseudo_boule`** at character 635. `bzprop:c2s2p5_ouvert_plein` is unmarked, at character 1510. (5) Build, sorry, axioms and scope are clean (build, scope).

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d6_pseudo_boule
labels.notes: MARK STANDS. pseudoBoule n M r = {N | ∃ Sg, IsMajoreSeg n r Sg M N} (PseudoBoules.lean:205). IsMajoreSeg (Mesure.lean:292) is Déf. 2 as marked. Its first conjunct, IsProjSegment n Sg M N (Classes.lean:168, Déf. 14), says that Sg is a CLOSED segment (Sphere.closedSeg in a compatible chart) with endpoints M and N, non-antipodal. The second conjunct says that Sg lies in a segment (A, B) of V relative to which every compatible chart gives a measure < r. This is « il existe au moins un segment fermé d'extrémités M, N, majoré par r » (l.411–415) word for word. « d'extrémités M, N » is unordered and the Lean is ordered, but mem_pseudoBoule_comm (via IsMajoreSeg.symm) makes the order immaterial. r : ℝ extends the paper's domain (« positif »). For a definition this is harmless: on the paper's domain the two agree, whether positif means r > 0 or r ≥ 0, and for r ≤ 0 the set is ∅ (pseudoBoule_eq_empty_of_nonpos). The parenthetical « (r ≥ 0) » at l.76 is an unflagged reading (finding 1), but it does not affect the mark. Dimension 0: pseudoBoule 0 M r = ∅ (pseudoBoule_dim_zero) is not an artefact of Déf. 6. It is Déf. 2's behaviour there (not_isMajoreSeg_dim_zero, which rests on Déf. 1 giving (x, x, x, x) no value), and Déf. 6 inherits it with no further choice. The same holds for Déf. 3 and Déf. 4, which were marked: curation.toml rows 303–321, and Déf. 3's note says that OQ-45 « bears on the properties row, not on this definition ». OQ-45's own text (DECISIONS.md:201) says that Déf. 2–4 « would become partial in dimension 0 only under (b) read as a correction ». Déf. 6 sits in exactly that position, and under any OQ-45 outcome it changes with Déf. 2 and needs no edit of its own. Recommendation: keep the mark, and add Déf. 6 to OQ-45's text beside Déf. 2–4 (finding 4). The transcription (l.411–415, 417–418, 420–423, 425–429, 431–435) was checked against the page image (PDF p. 25). It matches: « r un nombre réel positif », « lcs » (the image reads lcs, although the OCR layer reads « les »), and « r un nombre réel ». The unlabelled lemmas are correct. pseudoBoule_ouvert_connexe gives IsOpen ∧ IsPreconnected for every n and r. isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff gives IsConnected ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < r. hasBasis_pseudoBoule gives (𝓝 M).HasBasis (0 < ·) (pseudoBoule n M) on corpsInterior K for IsCorpsConvexeS n K under [NeZero n] (disclosed, ⚠ strengthened). baseVoisinagesPrinted_iff (↔ 0 < n) has the genuine witness {x} ⊆ S(0), whose pseudo-balls are empty. The REPORT's three findings on the sentences are accurate and stated as gaps, not as errors. (a) « cf. 3°, 5° »: 5° is a limsup bound on segments that already exist. It does not produce a segment (M, N′) for N′ near N, which openness needs. The proof gets that segment from the chart of the majorising segment (isOpen_pseudoBoule, eventually_exists_projMeasure_lt). (b) « il résulte du 6° »: continuity and « nulle si et seulement si M = N » alone do not make small balls small, since a continuous function vanishing only at M can tend to 0 elsewhere. The proof adds the connectedness of the balls and local compactness, and that argument is sound. (c) Dimension-0 failure of sentence 2: genuine under Déf. 1's convention (OQ-45).

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p5_ouvert_plein
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED and status partial. ouvert_plein (PseudoBoules.lean:494) assumes [TopologicalSpace V] [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] [PreconnectedSpace V], with V in any universe and no T2 or countability (weaker than the paper; ⚠ weakened). It also assumes IsOpen U, U.Nonempty, 0 < r and ∀ M ∈ U, pseudoBoule n M r ⊆ U, and concludes U = univ. That is the paper's statement plus 0 < r, in every dimension (n = 0 through subsingleton_dim_zero). It is not vacuous: V = S(n) with U = univ satisfies the hypotheses. eq_univ_of_forall_pseudoBoule_subset drops IsOpen U, and the REPORT's second finding (openness is redundant once r > 0) is true (isOpen_of_forall_pseudoBoule_subset). The clopen proof uses Prop. 3 (voisinage_majore, strict) and no broken line. OuvertPleinPrinted n (l.541) has the printed shape: V : Type, T2, ConnectedSpace and SecondCountableTopology (CAMPAIGN's standing reading of « variété »), U open and non-empty, ∀ r : ℝ, conclusion U = univ. ouvertPleinPrinted_iff (↔ n = 0) is correctly proved. Its witness S(n) ∖ {x} with r = 0 satisfies the Lean predicate, because S(n) is connected for n ≥ 1 (connectedSpace_S) and second countable. BUT it satisfies the paper's hypotheses only if a pseudo-ball of radius 0 is a Déf. 6 object, that is, only if « r un nombre réel positif » includes 0. Negative r lies outside Déf. 6 under either reading of « positif ». The paper's own usage reads « positif » as > 0 (finding 1). Under that convention Prop. 5's r is a Déf. 6 radius, so r > 0, and ouvert_plein is Prop. 5 as printed in every dimension. The finding « false as printed for every r ≤ 0 » is therefore not established and should not go to the author as a fact. Recommendation: keep the row unmarked until the reading of « positif » is ruled (an OQ with the evidence of finding 1, or the existing REPORT question reworded). If the ruling is > 0, mark Benzecri.ouvert_plein with no Lean change. Only under « positif » = ≥ 0 (Bourbaki) is ouvert_plein_counterexample a genuine counterexample, at r = 0.

lemmas_checked.pseudoBoule_ouvert_connexe: IsOpen ∧ IsPreconnected, for every n and every r. isPreconnected_pseudoBoule uses isPreconnected_of_forall with M as base point, and each majorised segment through M lies in the ball (IsMajoreSeg.subset_pseudoBoule, via exists_subset_left and pseudoLength_mono, which is 3°).
lemmas_checked.isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff: IsConnected (pseudoBoule n M r) ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < r. Correct. With nonempty_pseudoBoule_iff it settles the sentence under either reading of « connexe ».
lemmas_checked.hasBasis_pseudoBoule: HasBasis on 𝓝 M with index 0 < r, for V = corpsInterior K and IsCorpsConvexeS n K, under [NeZero n]. The proof (compact neighbourhood, positive minimum of l_V(M, ·) on its frontier, connected ball) is sound. In V = int K, mem_pseudoBoule_corpsInterior_iff identifies the ball with {N | hilbertLength K M N < r}.
lemmas_checked.baseVoisinagesPrinted_iff: ↔ 0 < n, over every convex body K of S(n) and every M in int K. For n = 0 the witness is {x} (isCorpsConvexeS_singleton_S0, accepted in T-bz-c2-hilbert AUDIT-1), whose pseudo-balls are empty. Genuine under Déf. 1's convention, so this is OQ-45 and not OQ-56 (finding 2).
lemmas_checked.isMajoreSeg_iff_pseudoLength_lt: IsMajoreSeg n k Sg M N ↔ pseudoLength n Sg M N < k. Correct (Déf. 3 is an infimum over the real numbers k that majorise). A candidate to move upstream, as the REPORT says. It overlaps the ← direction of Lignes.lean's exists_isMajoreSeg_of_pseudoLength_lt (another closer's file, read-only, no name clash found).
lemmas_checked.discreteTopology_dim_zero / subsingleton: Stated correctly. connectedSpace_S goes through S.homeomorphEuclideanSphere and Mathlib's isConnected_sphere.

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[1].findings[0], labels[1].hypotheses[2] and questions[0], labels[0].hypotheses[1] and questions[0]; PseudoBoules.lean:24, :76 (« (r ≥ 0) »), :85, :90–96 (SCOPE), :527–528 (ouvert_plein_counterexample docstring), :539–548 (OuvertPleinPrinted / ouvertPleinPrinted_iff docstrings)
findings.what: The finding « Prop. 5 is false as printed for every r ≤ 0 » would go to the author as a fact, but it rests on an unflagged reading that the paper's own usage contradicts. Prop. 5 speaks of « la pseudo-boule de centre M et de rayon r ». Déf. 6 defines that set only for « r un nombre réel positif ». A negative r is outside Déf. 6 under any reading; the Lean's pseudoBoule is extended to every real r, which is harmless for the definition but is not the paper. So the counterexample depends entirely on r = 0, and the REPORT asserts as fact that r = 0 is « positif » in Déf. 6's sense, so that « reading r as in Déf. 6 does not save it ». Benzécri's usage reads « positif » as > 0. (i) Ch. 1 Déf. 3 (ch1 l.167–169) prints « Le groupe multiplicatif ℝ⁺ … groupe des homothéties positives », which must be ]0, ∞[. The strict library's S(E) = Module.Ray already reads it so. (ii) Ch. 1 l.203–206: an OPEN hemisphere has F(H) = l⁻¹(ℝ⁺), and l is defined « à un multiplicateur positif près ». Benzecri/Projective/Hemisphere.lean reads this as 0 < l v. (iii) Ch. 1 l.299 and l.527 (« Le groupe ℝ⁺ des réels positifs ») and l.751 likewise. (iv) Ch. 2 l.82 writes « positif ou nul » for the pseudo-length, which would be redundant if « positif » meant ≥ 0. (v) Ch. 2 l.669, « Soit k un nombre réel positif … ma/ab < k »: taking M = A gives 0 < k, so k > 0 is needed. « strictement positif » at ch2 l.366, 383 and 470 shows that the usage is not uniform, but no occurrence shows « positif » including 0. Under the paper's convention, Prop. 5's r is a Déf. 6 radius, so r > 0. Benzecri.ouvert_plein is then Prop. 5 as printed in every dimension, and ouvert_plein_counterexample does not satisfy the paper's hypotheses. The printed proof (broken lines of r-majorised segments, which Prop. 4 provides for k > 0) is consistent with that reading. The Lean statements are all correct. The error is in the claim about the paper: it is at best unsupported, and most probably false.
findings.fix: No Lean statement changes. Withdraw « false as printed » as a finding and restate it as a reading or question. Proposed wording: « Prop. 5's r is a Déf. 6 radius. In the paper's usage « positif » is r > 0 (ch1 Déf. 3's multiplicative group ℝ⁺, ch1 l.205, ch2 l.82, l.669), and under it Prop. 5 holds as printed in every dimension (Benzecri.ouvert_plein). Only if « positif » is read as ≥ 0 (Bourbaki) does r = 0 refute it (ouvert_plein_counterexample, ouvertPleinPrinted_iff). Negative radii are outside Déf. 6 under either reading. » In the file: l.76, « (r ≥ 0) » becomes « (r > 0 in the paper's usage, r ≥ 0 under Bourbaki's; question) ». l.85 becomes « ✓ carried: 0 < r, r being a Déf. 6 radius (question) ». Rewrite l.24 and SCOPE l.90–96 conditionally. In the docstrings at l.527–528 and l.539–548, replace « as printed » and « a « nombre réel positif » in the sense of Déf. 6 » with « Prop. 5 with pseudoBoule extended to every real radius; a counterexample to the paper only if « positif » includes 0 ». Routing: the row stays partial and unmarked until the author rules on « positif » (a new OQ with the evidence above). If the ruling is > 0, the mark goes on Benzecri.ouvert_plein unchanged.

findings.where: PseudoBoules.lean:82 (checklist « Sentence 2: the dimension … (baseVoisinagesPrinted_iff; OQ-45, OQ-56) »)
findings.what: The docstring cites OQ-56 for the dimension-0 failure of the basis sentence, but REPORT labels[0].findings[2] says « OQ-56 does not bear on it ». The REPORT is right. At n = 0 the sentence fails because every pseudo-ball is empty (Déf. 1's convention, OQ-45), and Prop. 2's reading of « ne s'annule que sur la diagonale » plays no part.

The « connexe » question motivates the Bourbaki reading by saying that the non-empty reading « fails for r = 0, which Déf. 6's « r un nombre réel positif » allows ». This inherits the convention error of finding 1. With « positif » = > 0, the non-empty reading (IsConnected) holds for every Déf. 6 radius once n ≥ 1 (isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff), so the reading matters only in dimension 0 (OQ-45). It is not a narrowing: both forms are proved, so the Lean is at least the paper under either reading.
findings.fix: Reword as: « Under the non-empty reading the sentence holds for every Déf. 6 radius when n ≥ 1 (isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff), and fails only at n = 0 (OQ-45), and at r = 0 if « positif » includes 0. Under Bourbaki's reading it holds in every dimension (pseudoBoule_ouvert_connexe). »
